- **Member onboarding & first 30 days** – no documented sequence for intake forms, induction class, goal-setting, buddy/coach assignment

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**Audit first, then design:**
- Spend 2 hours with your top 3 coaches asking: "What do members actually ask for?" and "What takes up most of your time?" This kills guesswork. Your menu should reflect what's *already selling*, not what sounds good.

**Split into two docs with ruthless clarity:**
- **Coach version:** Exactly what you offer (class types, PT packages, nutrition coaching, whatever), margin per service, upsell sequence (how does someone go from group class → PT → nutrition?). This drives consistency and prevents undercutting.
- **Member version:** Clean, benefit-focused copy. "Small Group Training (4 people max)" → "*Get personalized form checks + tailored progressions* — £X/session or £Y/month." Include what's bundled (locker access, app, community events).

**Price anchoring move:**
- List your *premium* option first (e.g., 1:1 coaching), then show the "good middle ground" (small group). Psychology works—people anchor to the first price they see. Test this with 10 members before finalizing.

**Lock in a simple decision tree:**
- Create a one-page flowchart: "New member?" → "Beginner class" → "After 4 weeks, offer PT assessment." This removes coach guesswork and creates predictable upgrade paths. Saves time *and* money left on the table.

**Live date this week:**
- Pick Friday to launch internally. Coaches need to live it before members see it. Any friction now = you fix it before it hits your sales funnel.

## REVENUE: ARREST THE MEMBER VALUE COLLAPSE

• **Rev/member has crashed from £145 (July) to £100 (August) — a 31% drop in 4 weeks.** Active members rose to 162 (+26 from July) but revenue only grew £16,160 vs £19,764, meaning you're acquiring bodies at a discount or losing high-value members. Audit your June–August pricing & membership tier mix: if you're running summer promotions, lock an end date and return standard pricing September 1st immediately.

• **Churn spiked to 12.8% in May, then normalised.** August is back to 5.6%, so retention mechanics are working — but those May dropouts cost you 17 lost members that month. Run a 30-day win-back campaign on May churners (discounted 3-month restart) before they ghost completely; they're cheaper to re-acquire than cold traffic.

• **Target: restore Rev/member to £130+ by end of September** (= £21k+ revenue at 162 members). Lever: (1) kill any discount memberships still active; (2) introduce a £20/month "class pack add-on" (personal training drop-ins, peak-hours premium access, or nutrition modules) to existing members — target 20% uptake = +£636/month at 162 members with zero churn cost.

---

## EXPENSES: AUGUST CASH OUT IS 55% ABOVE JULY (RED FLAG)

• **Cash outflows: £18,497 (July) → £28,693 (August) — a £10k spike (+55%) with no corresponding revenue jump.** Post-relocation stabilisation should have *reduced* opex. Investigate immediately: (1) one-off stock/equipment buys? (2) supplier payment batching? (3) payroll creep (staffing hours over budget for summer peak)? Get a line-by-line from Starling for July & August and flag any recurring new line items.

• **Last 3 months (Jun–Aug) avg revenue £17,363 vs prior 3 (Feb–Apr, excluding relocation distortion from April) avg £15,525 — +12% revenue growth.** But cash burn in June and August wiped profits. If payroll or utilities spiked post-relocation, model them now and cut one discretionary cost (e.g. unused software subscriptions, over-staffing on quiet shifts, expensive cleaning contract) to reclaim £2–3k/month.
